doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

chapter: Race, audiences and the jazz scene
title: Aging festival audiences and bringing in younger listeners
summary: Rowe worries about young listeners; Robinson notes the broad-age crowd at the Robinson event.

venues.name: Jackie Robinson Foundation Afternoon for Jazz

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: It’s a little scary for the future of some of this music when you look at the audience and I doubt there’s many people at this festival that are under 55 you know. And you wonder, are there going to be younger listeners that at least come in to this particular style of music?

Right. Well there again at the Jackie Robinson Festival there were all ages there. There were families and there were little kids and there were young amateur players, and it was a wider segment. So we need to bring those people in. I mean that would be great if we could bring those people in. Of course something like this, I don’t know, I’m not the type to be able to put something like this together, but I think it ought to be possible somehow to bring in families and younger people. Because it happens in these other kind of situations.
